title: Employee Basic Pay Details — Create / Edit
overviewHtml:
One wage type and amount within a basic pay record — for example basic salary, housing allowance or transport allowance. Payroll calculates each wage type from the detail line of the basic pay in force on the pay date.

A basic pay record can hold each wage type only once.

fields.label: EmployeeBasicPayId
fields.html: What it is. The basic pay record this line belongs to.

fields.label: WageTypeId
fields.rules: Required. Chosen from Wage Type master data.
fields.html:
What it is. The pay element this line pays.

Example. Basic Salary

Why it matters. Each wage type can appear once per basic pay record.

fields.label: Amount
fields.html:
What it is. The rate for this wage type, per the basic pay's pay interval.

Example. 850.000

Why it matters. Payroll uses it as the monthly, daily or hourly rate for this wage type, and it is carried into the cost and journal postings.

fields.label: CurrencyId
fields.rules: Required. Chosen from Currency master data.
fields.html:
What it is. The currency of the amount.

Example. KWD

Why it matters. The journal voucher export reads it to post the employee's pay in this currency.

fields.label: DependantUnit
fields.html:
What it is. Whether this line depends on another wage type, and how.

Example. Percentage

Why it matters. Used only when a dependent wage type is chosen.

fields.label: DependantNumber
fields.html:
What it is. The percentage of the dependent wage type's amount.

Example. 25

fields.label: DependantWageTypeId
fields.rules: Optional. Chosen from Wage Type master data.
fields.html:
What it is. Another wage type this line is calculated from.

Example. Basic Salary
fields.adminHtml: When this is set, payroll calculates the percentage of that wage type's amount but stores the result in the payroll line's number, not its amount — behaviour carried over from the legacy system. The line does not currently pay the calculated percentage.
